articles.title: Nucleation of water ice under weak ionization via clustering on negative ions
articles.summary: Water-ice grains are shown to form spontaneously in a cold, weakly-ionized laboratory plasma with trace water admixture when neutrals and ions are cooled below $\sim$200 K. Time-resolved ion mass spectrometry provides separate detection of clusters of water molecules on both positive and negative ions. articles.title: Spectral Constraints on Line-Seed Inverse-Compton Models for the MeV Feature in GRB 221009A
articles.summary: We investigate inverse-Compton (IC) scattering of atomic and molecular line photons as an explanation of the evolving MeV spectral feature observed by Fermi-GBM in GRB 221009A. articles.title: Analysis Methodology of the Search for Ultrahigh Energy Neutrinos in 10.6 Years of Askaryan Radio Array Data
articles.summary: The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA) is an in-ice radio observatory at the South Pole designed to detect ultrahigh energy (UHE) neutrinos through Askaryan emission produced by interactions of neutrinos and their secondary particles. In this paper, we present the detailed methodology of the first array-wide search for a diffuse UHE neutrino flux using data from all five ARA stations. articles.title: New Constraints on the Ultrahigh Energy Neutrino Flux from the First Array-Wide Search with the Askaryan Radio Array
articles.summary: Ultrahigh energy neutrinos ($E_ν\gtrsim 100$ PeV) are detectable through Askaryan emission---the nanosecond-scale radio impulse emitted by relativistic particle cascades in a dielectric medium. The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA), an Askaryan detector array located at the South Pole, has been taking data for more than a decade. We present the first array-wide search for diffuse ultrahigh energy neutrinos with ARA. The search found no events on an expected background of $0.13\pm0.01\text{ (stat.)}^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\text{ (syst.)}$ events. articles.title: Perturbative QCD Constraints on Hot Neutron-Star Matter
articles.summary: Perturbative QCD, supplemented only by thermodynamic consistency, causality, and mechanical stability, constrains the equation of state of dense matter far below the densities at which the perturbative expansion itself converges. articles.summary: I search the single-epoch detections of the NOIRLab Source Catalog DR2 (DECam, 2012-2019) for outer Solar System objects. articles.title: Relativistic tidal response and mode excitation in neutron-star binaries
articles.summary: Tidal excitation links gravitational-wave emission to the internal dynamics of neutron stars. We study the dynamical tidal response of nonrotating stars with composition stratification, elastic crusts and possible first-order phase transitions. articles.title: Unveiling the Extreme Universe with Recent IACT Discoveries
articles.summary: Very-high-energy (VHE, $E \gtrsim 50$\,GeV) $γ$-ray astronomy has evolved into an indispensable pillar of modern astroparticle physics, offering a direct view of non-thermal particle acceleration, cosmic-ray origins, and fundamental physics. articles.title: Probing for anisotropies at different angular scales in the arrival directions of the cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory
articles.summary: Studies of the arrival-direction distribution of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays are crucial for revealing their origin. In this work, we investigate the distribution of the arrival directions of events detected with the Pierre Auger Observatory over different angular scales. To do this, we adopt a novel method where we use a von Mises--Fisher distribution to model the excesses with respect to isotropic expectations. This method allows us to study the distribution of arrival directions over different angular scales consistently and simultaneously. articles.title: Spectral-Timing Evolution of the Black Hole X-ray Binary LMC X-3: An XPoSat View
articles.summary: LMC X-3 is a persistent black hole high-mass X-ray binary and serves as an important laboratory for studying accretion disk evolution across different spectral states. We present a spectral-timing analysis of XPoSat/XSPECT observations of LMC X--3 obtained during 2024 and 2025. Using broadband X-ray light curves, hardness diagnostics, power spectral analysis, and spectral modeling, we investigate the long-term evolution of the source across multiple epochs. articles.title: A large radiatively loud anti-glitch in 1E 2259+586 with a protracted recovery
articles.summary: Context. Anti-glitches are rare and enigmatic timing anomalies. High-cadence monitoring has revealed radiatively quiet anti-glitches in several pulsar populations, but radiatively loud anti-glitches and their links to magnetospheric activity remain poorly understood. Aims. We characterize a new, large anti-glitch in the magnetar 1E 2259+586 and compare its phenomenology with other magnetars. Methods. articles.title: Empirical constraints on cosmic-ray scattering in NGC 1333 from dust polarisation
articles.summary: Cosmic rays (CRs) regulate molecular-cloud ionization and chemistry. Gyro-resonant scattering by magnetic fluctuations sets their mean free path and, on larger scales, their effective diffusion coefficient. articles.title: Search Method for Continuous Gravitational Waves from Rotating Neutron Stars in Highly Eccentric Wide Orbits
articles.summary: Recent results from the Gaia third data release have highlighted 21 potential neutron stars candidates in wide, highly-eccentric binary systems and provide estimates of their orbital parameters. To this extent, we have computed a frequency metric to place templates in the parameter space accounting for uncertainties on the orbital parameters. articles.title: The Brown Dwarf Desert is a Mass-Ratio Desert: Astrometric Demographics of 63,254 Stars
articles.summary: Brown dwarfs are rare as close companions to stars compared to planets and stellar companions, a paucity known as the brown dwarf desert. Whether the desert sits at a fixed companion mass or a fixed companion-to-star mass-ratio $q$ has been difficult to test, because microlensing, radial velocities, and direct imaging have sampled comparatively narrow slices of stellar mass and separation. Here we apply a novel joint-modelling method to Hipparcos and Gaia DR2/DR3 astrometry from 63,254 stars to complete this picture with a sample 1-2 orders of magnitude larger than those of previous wide-orbit demographic studies. articles.title: Search for a Dispersion Measure Excess Toward Nearby Galaxy Halos Using Fast Radio Bursts from the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog
articles.summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) probe foreground ionized baryons via their dispersion measures (DM). Using 1748 sub-arcminute-localized sources from the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog, we conduct a statistical stacking study of the circumgalactic media (CGM) of nearby galaxies by analyzing the DMs of FRBs whose sightlines intersect foreground halos. articles.title: The Tierras Observatory: Ultra-Precise Photometry for Characterizing Exoplanets and Their Host Stars
articles.summary: The Tierras Observatory is a fully robotic 1.3-m telescope at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory in southern Arizona. Tierras achieves sub-part-per-thousand (ppt) photometric precision on two timescales: intra-night, to detect and characterize transits of planets around nearby mid-to-late M dwarfs, and night-to-night across an observing season, to characterize the long-term variability of their host stars. articles.title: AGN Feedback Turbulence in Cool-core Clusters: Evidence from XRISM
articles.summary: The XRISM X-ray Observatory has revealed evidence for a "double-cascade" scenario in the Perseus cluster, in which active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback and mergers drive turbulence over distinct radial ranges and spatial scales. Whether this gas kinematic feature is common among cool-core clusters remains unclear. Here, we revisit XRISM observations of A1795 and A2029 to investigate the signatures of AGN feedback and their contribution to the gas velocity fields. articles.title: Joint Gaia-Hipparcos astrometry, RV, and Imaging posteriors from the G23H Hipparcos sample
articles.summary: We present uniform posteriors indicating the presence or absence of stellar and planetary companions over a sample of $10^5$ stars in Hipparcos and Gaia. We use the "G23H" catalog to fit a model that incorporates absolute astrometry constraints from Hipparcos, Gaia DR2, and Gaia DR3, as well as Gaia DR3 photometry, excess RV variability, and includes information from the presence or absence of common-proper motion companions. articles.title: MarsNet: Learning the Martian Atmosphere from Observations Alone
articles.summary: We present MarsNet, a machine-learned model of the Martian atmosphere trained only on observations. articles.title: GRB 241030A: A fallback-accreting magnetar description of the early X-ray emission
articles.summary: The bright, variable early X-ray emission of GRB~241030A at $z=1.411$ motivates investigating continued central-engine activity before the smoother afterglow emerges. articles.summary: Young protoplanetary disks have received increasing attention in recent years, due to observations revealing the presence of substructures in disks younger than one million years, suggesting that planet formation may begin earlier than previously thought. Other recent observations have provided new insights into the evolution of gas and dust in these early stages, enabling comparisons with evolved Class II disks. articles.title: The Swift/UVOT Observation Campaign of Comet C/2013 US10 (Catalina) and Near-nucleus UV Excess
articles.summary: We present results of a multi-wavelength extended monitoring campaign of dynamically new long-period comet C/2013 US$_{10}$ (Catalina), captured with the Ultraviolet and Optical Telescope (UVOT) on board the Swift spacecraft covering 5.8 AU inbound to 5 AU outbound. articles.title: The Edge of the Warm Corona in Active Galactic Nuclei
articles.summary: A model of warm, dissipative corona on top of an accretion disk is investigated, to explain the soft X-ray excess (SXE) emission observed in active galactic nuclei (AGN). articles.title: The compositional link between rocky exoplanets and their host stars is consistent with Earth-like devolatilization
articles.summary: Previous work found a higher bulk iron-to-silicon (Fe/Si) ratio in rocky exoplanets relative to their host star, traditionally explained by iron enrichment. We explore whether these elemental molar ratios are consistent with a devolatilization trend. articles.summary: Thanks to recent measurements by space and ground-level detectors, the energy spectra of cosmic ray protons and helium nuclei are now known with good precision over a broad energy range extending for more than six orders of magnitude, from a few GeV to approximately 10PeV. articles.title: VLT and Keck recovery and characterisation of 2025 SC$_{79}$: linking 'Ayló'chaxnim and Atira asteroids
articles.summary: Asteroids near the boundary between the Atira and 'Ayló'chaxnim classes can trace dynamical links between the two populations, but their small solar elongations make recovery and physical characterisation difficult. articles.title: Effects of a Nuclear Detonation in Low Earth Orbit
articles.summary: More than 13,000 satellites operate in low Earth orbit (LEO), and concern has grown that nuclear weapons could be used in space to target them. articles.title: Superorbital period evolution of Hercules X-1
articles.summary: Context. Hercules X-1 (Her X-1) is a well-studied X-ray binary exhibiting superorbital modulation of its X-ray flux. We investigated the long-term trend of the superorbital modulation using more recent, uninterrupted data from 1995-2025 to identify features that may favour or disfavour the proposed mechanisms. articles.title: Forecasting Fundamental-Plane Tests of Intermediate-mass Black Holes in Radio-selected Dwarf Galaxies
articles.summary: A radio/X-ray Fundamental Plane (FP) test of an intermediate-mass black hole is informative only when the compact radio emission, hard X-rays, accretion state, and host association refer to the same accretor. articles.title: Advances in High-Precision Astrometry for Exoplanet Detection for Astrometric Missions
articles.summary: High-precision astrometry is a cornerstone for detecting Earth-like exoplanets in the habitable zones of nearby solar-type stars and probing the nature of dark matter in galactic environments. articles.title: A possible connection between the ridge and hypotenuse in the bispectrum of black hole X-ray binaries through quasi-periodic modulation
articles.summary: Quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in black-hole X-ray binaries show nonlinear coupling with broadband variability, producing characteristic ridge, hypotenuse, and web-like structures in the bicoherence. articles.title: Fundamental Noise Processes in Pulsar Timing

articles.title: Mathematical foundations and numerical simulations of BDNK hydrodynamics: from heavy-ion collisions to astrophysics
articles.summary: We present new developments in the mathematical foundations and numerical simulations of the causal and stable first-order relativistic viscous hydrodynamic theory by Bemfica, Disconzi, Noronha, and Kovtun (BDNK) in general spacetimes. articles.title: XMM-Newton observations of the highest field polar AR UMa: An extreme case of soft-blobby accretion
articles.summary: (Context) The X-ray spectra of magnetic cataclysmic variables (MCVs) with extreme magnetic fields, the polars, often exhibit a prominent soft X-ray excess attributed to buried shocks. articles.title: Constraints on Cosmic-Rays and the MeV Emission from Jupiter's Atmosphere
articles.summary: The Cosmic $γ$-ray Background (CGB) in the MeV regime remains among the least understood components of diffuse cosmic radiation, primarily due to instrumental limitations in detecting faint isotropic emission at MeV energies. articles.title: Validation of Habitable Zone Limits with a New Radiative-Convective Equilibrium Climate Model
articles.summary: The habitable zone (HZ) boundaries calculated with the Clima one-dimensional radiative-convective equilibrium (RCE) model have served as a standard reference for exoplanet target selection for three decades, but they have never been independently validated with a comparable model. articles.title: CO gaps in cold transition disks around low-mass stars
articles.summary: Transition disks with large inner dust cavities are promising targets to study planet formation, as these disks are likely hosting massive planetary companions. articles.title: Activity of the ejected galactic nuclei and cosmic rays
articles.summary: The double and triple approaches of supermassive central black holes are a fairly common process in the hierarchical picture of galaxy formation. articles.title: GW230729\_082317 and GW231118\_005626: A Candidate of Hierarchical Triple Mergers
articles.summary: Hierarchical triple mergers denote a sequential merger process in which the black hole remnant from an initial binary merger subsequently merges with a third black hole. In this study, we identify a related pair of binary black hole mergers, GW230729\_082317 and GW231118\_005626, which exhibit consistent sky localization and luminosity distances; the latter is identified as a candidate hierarchical merger binary back holes. articles.title: Quasi-spherical fallback in binary neutron-star mergers: fuel and obstacle for extended emission
articles.summary: Extended emission (EE) lasting hundreds of seconds has been observed in a fraction of short gamma-ray bursts (sGRB) containing both nonthermal and thermal components, and representing a significant puzzle for models involving binary neutron stars (BNSs). articles.title: BeAR: The Bern Atmospheric Retrieval code - A GPU-accelerated framework for low-resolution, high-resolution, and joint retrievals of exoplanet atmospheres
articles.summary: We present BeAR, the Bern Atmospheric Retrieval code and successor of Helios-r, and its new high-resolution cross-correlation framework for emission and transmission spectra. articles.summary: We present an analysis of JADES-GS-BD-5, an extremely cold Y dwarf identified in the JADES/GOODS-South field. articles.title: The complex periodic variability of PKS 0301-243: hints of a supermassive black hole binary candidate
articles.summary: In hierarchical galaxy formation, supermassive black hole binaries are a ubiquitous consequence of frequent galaxy mergers, yet subparsec binaries remain difficult to be confirmed. articles.summary: Space-based astrometric missions such as Hipparcos and Gaia rely on one-dimensional scanning strategies that couple the measured signals with both observation times and scanning geometry. articles.summary: Previous studies combined rotation periods derived from Kepler photometry, stellar parameters from previous Gaia Data Releases, and planet hosts from the NASA Exoplanet Archive to conclude that statistically planet-hosting stars rotate slower than stars without detected planets. articles.summary: We revisit the impact of electroweak (EW) radiative corrections on the kinematic distributions of charged leptons in neutrino-induced charged-current (CC) deep inelastic scattering (DIS). articles.summary: We present results from a stellar occultation by the asteroid (623) Chimaera on October 21st, 2025, when it passed in front of V magnitude 13.86 star UCAC4 626-004193. articles.title: Mass loss in AF supergiants: At the verge of the Eddington limit and still with weak line-driven winds
articles.summary: We study global atmosphere models of AF supergiants. articles.title: Multi-epoch monitoring of the faint northern component in 3C 84 during 2016-2021
articles.summary: We present the results of multi-epoch very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) observations of the sub-parsec-scale northern jet component of 3C 84 (known as the N1 component) at 7 mm from 2016 to 2021. articles.summary: Blazars are active galactic nuclei with relativistic jets closely aligned with our line of sight, producing Doppler-boosted emission from radio to gamma rays. articles.summary: Using the Green Bank Telescope, we discovered the 1.68-ms binary pulsar PSR J2053+6905.
